angles.title: A feeling that mattered and I can't say why
angles.audience: not yet known (the memo names no reader)

uses.quote: I had a feeling about something, like a mood more than an idea
But it felt like it mattered while I was walking, and I can't say why.
I just wanted to get the feeling down before it goes.

open_questions: What was the feeling? The memo calls it 'a mood more than an idea' but never names it.
Is the piece about the feeling itself, or about the not-knowing-why and the urge to catch it before it goes?
Who is it for: yourself, or readers who know that kind of unexplained mood?

angles.title: Days I walk
angles.audience: not yet known (the memo names no reader)

uses.quote: Maybe it's about how I feel different on days I walk.
something about routines, but I don't know what I would say about routines that people haven't already said a hundred times
It was about mornings, I think, or maybe about the walk.

open_questions: How do you feel different on days you walk? The memo says you do, not how.
What could you say about routines that hasn't 'already been said a hundred times'? You raise that worry yourself and don't answer it.
You also say 'maybe it's not about walking at all'. Is walking the subject, or only where the feeling showed up?

angles.title: The city on a morning walk
angles.audience: not yet known (the memo names no reader)

uses.quote: My sister says I should write about the city more, but I don't know which part of the city.
The light was nice. There were a lot of dogs out.
I could write about the dogs, but that seems silly.

open_questions: Which part of the city? The memo leaves that open.
Is this your idea or only your sister's? The memo gives it as her suggestion.
The light and the dogs are the only concrete details. You call the dogs 'silly'. Are they worth keeping, or just a way into the piece?
